questions.solution_text:
1. **Rearrange the rule to make $x^{2}$ the subject in terms of $y$**
$x=\dfrac{y}{3}$
$x^{2}=\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}$
2. **Evaluate $V=\pi\int_{c}^{d}x^{2}\,dy$**
$V=\pi\int_{0}^{6}\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}dy$
$= \pi\left[\dfrac{y^{3}}{27}\right]_{0}^{6}$
$= \pi\times\dfrac{216}{27}$
$= 8\pi\ \text{units}^{3}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Rearrange the rule to make $x^{2}$ the subject in terms of $y$**
$y=2\sqrt{x}$
$x=\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}$
$x^{2}=\dfrac{y^{4}}{16}$
2. **Identify the limits as the $y$ values $c$ and $d$**
At $x=0$, $y=0$; at $x=4$, $y=2\sqrt{4}=4$.
3. **Evaluate $V=\pi\int_{c}^{d}x^{2}\,dy$**
$V=\pi\int_{0}^{4}\dfrac{y^{4}}{16}dy$
$= \pi\left[\dfrac{y^{5}}{80}\right]_{0}^{4}$
$= \pi\times\dfrac{1024}{80}$
$= \dfrac{64\pi}{5}\ \text{units}^{3}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Rearrange the rule to make $x^{2}$ the subject in terms of $y$**
$x=\dfrac{y}{2}$
$x^{2}=\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}$
2. **Evaluate $V=\pi\int_{c}^{d}x^{2}\,dy$**
$V=\pi\int_{0}^{k}\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}dy$
$= \pi\left[\dfrac{y^{3}}{12}\right]_{0}^{k}$
$= \dfrac{\pi k^{3}}{12}$
Setting this equal to the given volume:
$\dfrac{\pi k^{3}}{12}=144\pi$
$k^{3}=1728$
$k=12$
